## Introduction

This unit provides a brief overview to the various course tools. 
**The main materials to get started with these tools are found on a separate website, as described below.**

## Learning Objectives

The specific learning objectives for this unit are:

-   Know what tools we are using in this course.
-   Know where to learn about these tools.


## Course Tools

Every data analysis project requires a set of tools to get the job done. The exact tools (e.g., what programming language or editor you use) are often not that important, but it is important that the tools support efficient and reproducible workflows. We'll discuss that in a lot of detail in this course. In this course, we will be using a variety of tools to help us perform data analyses in a modern, reproducible way. 

- We will use AI tools to help with many of the steps involved in data analysis projects.
-   We will use the [`R`](https://www.r-project.org/) software for coding.
-   We will use the [`Positron`](https://positron.posit.co/) integrated development environment (IDE) to write our code and generally manage our projects. You can use a different editor/IDE if you want (e.g. RStudio or VS Code or Emacs), but the instructions assume you are using Positron.
-   We will use [`Quarto`](https://quarto.org/), to create output in an efficient, easy and automated manner.
-   We will use [`Git`](https://git-scm.com/) and [`GitHub`](https://github.com/) for exercises and the project.



# Important notes

Over the years that I've been teaching the course, the tools used in the course changed. Noticeable changes are the following:

- The company now called **Posit** was formerly called **R Studio**. You will likely see the old label show up here and there. 
- The editor we used in the past for writing R code is called **R Studio.** R Studio still exists, but a lot of new development effort is going into Posit's new editor **Positron**. We'll focus on Positron. Mentions of R Studio might still happen here and there. (And really, either editor is fine.)
- **Quarto** is also fairly new. In the past we used **R Markdown**. Again, you might come across references to **R Markdown** in the course materials or online. Quarto and R Markdown share many similarities. Quarto is basically a newer/better/expanded version of R Markdown. R Markdown still works, but Quarto is more powerful, so it's the better option to use/learn it.
- In the past, I used a tool for Git/GitHub called **GitKraken**. I decided that it's not necessary to use another piece of software, so now I'm focusing on GitHub Desktop and the built-in GitHub support of Positron. Again, there might be some GitKraken references in the materials, and you can certainly check it out if you want.


# Learning the tools

For ease of maintaining the material, I decided to create a separate website that contains small courses/tutorials that introduce the various tools.

The website that contains these tutorials/mini-courses is called [Modeling and Data Science (MDS) Tools](https://andreashandel.github.io/mds-tools/).

:::{emphasis}
As preparation for MADA and the first assignment, go through the tutorials/mini-courses [on th MDS Tools website](https://andreashandel.github.io/mds-tools/). The **Portfolio** tutorial will be your first exercise.
:::
